headline: My Flight Has Been Circling Mumbai So Long That I’ve Started Farming Microgreens On My Tray Table
body:
I didn't think I would be a farmer by the time my flight from Bangalore finally touched down, but here I am, harvesting my third crop of arugula at 30,000 feet. When the captain announced that we were the 265th aircraft in a holding pattern due to congestion, I initially panicked. But after six hours of circling over the city, I realized that the consistent cabin temperature and the mild, artificial sunlight from the reading lamp were perfect for a window-seat garden.

It’s actually quite productive. The flight attendants were initially skeptical, but after I shared a handful of freshly sprouted radish microgreens with the purser, they’ve started viewing my tray table as a legitimate farm-to-sky initiative. I’ve even managed to trade a bunch of kale with the gentleman in 14B for his bag of pretzels, which I’m currently using as compost for my next batch of mustard greens.

I’m not even annoyed about the deferral of the flight cuts anymore. If we land now, I’ll lose my harvest to the customs officers, and I’ve really bonded with these sprouts. Honestly, if the ground authorities want to keep me in the air for another rotation, I’ve got enough organic potting soil in my carry-on to start growing heirloom tomatoes by the time we hit the evening landing window.
caption: POV: Your flight is just a flying salad bar now. Who knew airport congestion could be this sustainable? ✈️🌱🥗 #MumbaiAirport #AviationLife #Microgreens #AirTravel (satire)
